knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Gradient state leakage in non-differentiable operators
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Operators that produce non-floating-point outputs from gradient-enabled inputs may fail to clear autograd state, violating the dtype-based gradient contract.

risk_dimensions.shape: Degenerate, zero-dim, scalar, and high-rank tensor shapes may expose gradient-state metadata propagation errors.
risk_dimensions.dtype: Floating-point inputs that produce integer or non-floating-point outputs; boundaries between differentiable and non-differentiable dtypes.
risk_dimensions.device: CPU/accelerator transitions can expose inconsistent gradient-state handling in dtype-changing operations.
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Gradient-enabled tensors passed through non-differentiable operations; output requires_grad state persists incorrectly.

failure_mechanism.description: The operator returns an integer/non-floating tensor but does not clear the gradient flag, violating the API contract that only floating-point tensors should require gradients.

input_exploration: Construct floating-point tensors with requires_grad=True across multiple dtypes and devices
Apply non-differentiable operations that return integer or boolean outputs
Vary tensor shapes including scalar, zero-dim, and high-rank layouts
Explore gradient-enabled inputs with different memory layouts and stride patterns
constraint_awareness: Only floating-point tensors should require gradients
Integer and boolean outputs must have requires_grad=False
Autograd state must not leak through non-differentiable operators
Check output dtype before validating gradient state
oracle_strategy: Inspect output.requires_grad for non-floating-point outputs and report any True as Incorrect Output
Compare gradient-state metadata against the dtype-based API contract
Monitor for mismatches between output dtype and requires_grad flag

transferability.reason: The gradient-state contract applies broadly to any API that can return non-floating-point outputs; indexing, reduction, sorting, and selection operations may share similar autograd metadata propagation issues.

important_considerations: Probe gradient-state contracts for non-differentiable operations that change output dtype
Verify that non-floating-point outputs never require gradients
Include empty, scalar, degenerate, and high-rank tensors in test generation
Remember that gradient state is metadata and does not depend on numerical operation result
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that construct gradient-enabled floating-point inputs and route them through dtype-changing non-differentiable operators
Instead of copying the original argmax issue, generalize to any operation that returns integer, boolean, or index-valued tensors
Assert the output gradient state against the expected dtype-based contract and record mismatches as failures
